state.purpose: Assess a narrow set of presentation proposals for CanLang, whose intended work is CRUD-centered business SaaS running on workerd and written by AI. Favor adoption and economical unambiguous source while preserving one canonical interface to server business rules. The task ends with reviewable draft evidence; it does not build a rendering engine, language compiler or browser application architecture.
state.baseline: DESIGN 9/9.1 already provides canonical daisyUI controls, default HTMX interaction and a generated app shell. HTML, CSS-class and hx markup are not authored DSL escape hatches. Existing declarations cover pages, parent-aware record views, operation forms/actions, read results, preference settings and message localization. Current .mjs examples merely propose lowercase @canlang/ui server factories with a single props object and nested children arrays; async query/callback preparation and serialization have no implementation.
state.facts: Quoted technical examples reproduce the repository without alterations. CanDo selects its All/Today/Overdue query predicate from an enum preference, yet the shared table always has -created ordering. CanDo.md requires the due views stated order and MIGRATION.md line 176 records the missing ordering selection. The grammar currently permits fixed signed UI selectors. Two proposed replacements for that slot use either complete enum dispatch or a declared fallback and exceptional cases, keeping the record-view body in one place.
state.polling: The actual refresh operation takes locations:text[], admits members, and checks staff(actor) before sending WorkSources.work and inserting WorkView. Verified work_result completion later updates that record. Its read policy is members restricted to the requesting account. The actual WorkSourcesV1 method returns WorkBatch and declares no changed event. CanDo.md line 58 requires fresh SOURCE requests on changes or configured periods; reading WorkView over GET cannot make any such request. Current every(duration)/event/send facilities can supply mechanics after explicit provider-event and delegated-principal contracts exist, but trusted actor=null cannot call the guarded refresh as an impersonated member. Those missing integrations remain an app workflow question. Optional poll proposes a constant interval from 1s through 1h and no polling when absent: only authorized context/query-bound GET reads, no overlap, suspension for hidden/inactive content, authorized draft retention and revoked-data clearing. Read failures carry technical feedback distinct from stored source status; no business cache is required. Reject an ancestor/descendant pair of poll sites. A sole page attribute minimizes eligible headers but reads more content; enabling collection sites offers smaller reads with more source locations. Existing manual refresh/reload avoids scheduling expense and notation, at the cost of automatic display freshness.
state.ordering: Complete dispatch supplies an owned enum preference and exactly one nonempty signed selector-list arm per case. Every referenced field is checked for sortable/readable use; switching arms restarts pagination but retains valid filters and drafts. Default dispatch instead is a closed object containing by, default and cases, so exceptional arms can be shorter while later enum additions inherit that specified fallback. Both remain presentation query selection over static shapes, with appended record IDs, original element indices for arrays, nulls after values and no alteration to expression-query ordering. They require neither duplicating UI bodies across tabs nor exposing a programmable comparison callback.
state.datetime: According to the HTML Standard, datetime-local values lack offset information. CanLang already stores datetime as UTC, formats in business/team zones and defines gap rejection plus explicit fold choice in local_instant. The source hold and interview operations in the payload are their real signatures and checks. A uniform generated form can offer wall-clock inputs and one explicit IANA zone, starting with team.timezone or UTC if teamless; pinned conversion rejects gaps and obtains an explicit offset/instant choice for folds. Switching display zones keeps resolved instants unchanged and requires visible confirmation before reinterpreting unresolved wall-time drafts. Business operations receive normalized instants only. No business timezone parameter or saved preference is assigned by this presentation setting, and hidden/unrelated record zones are not guessed. Requiring offset-bearing RFC3339 input simplifies exact handling while making local scheduling harder. Adding an authored readable form-zone initializer gives precise resource defaults but enlarges grammar and binding semantics; current code does not already provide it.
state.filters: A finite uniform filter proposal allows one typed condition for each declared selector, conjoining selectors. eq/ne cover string-like scalars, booleans/enums and permitted identity references; ordered integer, decimal, duration, date, datetime and money also support lt/lte/gt/gte/between. Range ends are ordered and inclusive; other order operators take a single operand. Supported nullable selectors add is_null/not_null. Omitting a condition imposes no restriction; it does not mean null equality. Non-null comparisons skip nulls, and hidden data never participates in a null check. Money values carry an explicit shared endpoint currency, filter only that currency and never convert it. Exact numeric/temporal representations survive the control/wire path. Reject unknown field/op/envelope combinations and direct selectors of arrays, structural/union/json/file/secret/action data. Apply row/field policy before filtering, sort/count/export, excluding a row without the condition-required field grant rather than evaluating its private value. Keep literal declared-field search separate; share the contract with browser, MCP and exports. Equality/null alone has lower implementation scope but cannot supply promised date ranges; adding membership/string operators widens usefulness together with required type/security rules. No per-app source format is added for uniform filtering.
state.labels: The suggested standard instance text checks readable nonempty title:text first and name:text second, using only these exact identifiers; otherwise it combines the localized model caption with the complete opaque ID. Every choice has secondary full identity, so duplicate names and clipped suffix collisions remain distinguishable. The rule cannot fetch a private label, split arbitrary identifiers, follow unrelated references for a caption, inspect secrets or reveal directory emails. When an already-readable reference points to an unreadable target, only that reference identity/type may be presented. User/member labels are IDs unless canonical authorized identity display exists. Apply identical rules to pickers, references and preferences. Always showing IDs is smaller and predictable but cumbersome for users. A declared disclosure-checked record-label expression handles richer domain identities but introduces syntax and model-specific authoring. Existing label= declarations provide static captions only.
state.evidence: The primary documentation consulted is https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-trigger/ for periodic GET/visibility filtering, https://htmx.org/attributes/hx-sync/ for request coordination, and https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/input.html#local-date-and-time-state-(type=datetime-local) for local controls without offsets. Those documents establish available mechanisms, not tested workerd integration, safe data handling, wall-time conversion, draft survival or runtime performance. Repository evidence is DESIGN.md lines 160,183,318-336,476-494,524-559 and GRAMMAR.md lines 101-110,360-394, plus CanDo.md 35/58 and MIGRATION.md 176. Compilation, rendering and runtime localization are not available to validate these drafts.
state.constraints: Compare authored token burden, clarity, access safety, relevant CRUD usability and implementation obligations for each alternative. Server authority, original operation checks, one invocation surface, daisyUI/HTMX and existing preference/message restrictions are held constant. Do not credit GET reads with producing new source snapshots. Report your uncertainty without treating numerical cutoffs as permission or a correctness proof; withhold a choice if the described rules are inconsistent.

source_code.capability:
derive source_names():text[] = ["maintenance","accounts","onboarding","board","volunteering"]
  export capability WorkSourcesV1 version=1
   work(account:user,locations:text[]) -> WorkBatch
source_code.task_view:
tabs preferences.view
   table Task as task where preferences.view==all or (task.due!=null and ((preferences.view==today and local_date(task.due,team.timezone)==local_date(now,team.timezone)) or (preferences.view==overdue and task.due<now and not task.done))) columns=title,assignee,due,priority,done order=-created filter=location,assignee,priority,done defaults={location=preferences.location,done=preferences.done} search=title display=split
source_code.hold:
scenario hold(resource:Resource,customer:Customer,from:datetime label=label_RoomRequest_from,until:datetime label=label_RoomRequest_until,quantity:int,email:email,use_allowance:bool=false label=label_hold_use_allowance) by=authenticated label="Hold workspace"@{nl="Werkplek tijdelijk reserveren"}
   require actor.email_verified and customer.active and resource.location in customer.locations
   require (reservation_manager and can_work(actor,resource.location)) or (customer.kind==individual and owns(actor,customer)) or has_location_role(actor,customer,booker,resource.location) or has_location_role(actor,customer,administrator,resource.location)
   require from>=now and from<until and quantity>0 and until-from>=resource.minimum and (until-from)%resource.increment==0m
   require free(resource,from-resource.buffer_before,until+resource.buffer_after,quantity,null)
   do
    create Booking {parent=resource,customer,account=actor,email,from,until,quantity,rate=resource.hourly,total=resource.hourly*((until-from)/1h)*quantity,terms=resource.terms,refund_before=from-resource.refund_notice,reserved_from=from-resource.buffer_before,reserved_until=until+resource.buffer_after,expires=now+15m,source=operation.id} as booking
source_code.interview:
scenario schedule(candidate:Candidate,interviewer:Employee label=label_interviewer,from:datetime label=label_Interview_from,until:datetime label=label_Interview_until,timezone:timezone) by=recruiter label="Schedule interview"@{nl="Gesprek plannen"}
   require can_work(actor,candidate.parent.location) and candidate.stage in [applied,interview] and interviewer.active and from>=now and from<until
   do
    create Interview {parent=candidate,interviewer,from,until,timezone,source=operation.id} as interview
    send StaffSchedule.reserve {value={source=interview.source,employee=interviewer.user,location=candidate.parent.location.id,from,until,skill="interview",kind=interview,revision=interview.version}} as delivery

proposed_syntax.poll:
page /tasks/my-work title="My work"@{nl="Mijn werk"} poll=5s
 require members
 list WorkView as view where view.account==actor order=-view.requested
proposed_syntax.scoped_poll: list WorkView as view where view.account==actor order=-view.requested poll=5s

poll.instructions: Recommend a useful minimum for periodic presentation GETs, comparing target precision with source-surface size while never treating those reads as guarded refresh calls.

criteria.scoped: Allow a constant poll interval on a page or collection under one shared paused/authorized/nonconcurrent/draft-safe contract. WorkView can be targeted cheaply, although additional header positions and nested-site validation are necessary.
criteria.page_only: Confine the periodic GET attribute to page declarations. The allowable location is simpler and covers any page read view, but more regions may be evaluated per request.
criteria.manual: Retain only today's explicit operation controls and user page reload. There is no new syntax or periodic read load, and automatic screen updates remain unavailable.
criteria.unresolved: Defer a polling surface when authorization and editable-state retention cannot be expressed with bounded rules.

order.instructions: Decide how the current collection-order attribute should choose static sort fields from a saved enum without reauthoring its child UI.

criteria.exhaustive: Require a selector/map arm for every enum case. Future additions must be handled and there is no implicit fallback, at the expense of restating identical small selector lists.
criteria.fallback: Allow one checked default ordering and a subset of exceptional cases in by/default/cases. Shared order arms need less repetition, while later cases take the explicitly declared default automatically.
criteria.unresolved: Reserve the ordering decision until either bounded dispatch contract can support checked query and cursor behavior.

datetime.instructions: Determine which datetime control policy gives a clear instant with acceptable authoring and local-calendar usability costs.

criteria.shared_zone: Provide common wall-clock fields with an explicit team/UTC-initialized IANA choice and fold disambiguation. No source attribute is needed, though exact zone conversion must be built and resource/business-field associations are intentionally not guessed.
criteria.offset_input: Collect explicit RFC3339 offsets directly instead of initializing local-zone controls. Parsing is exact and less conversion work is required, but clock-based booking is less convenient.
criteria.authored_zone: Add a checked readable-context zone attribute to seed those same wall-time controls. Resource defaults become precise, with extra declaration/binding/disclosure obligations.
criteria.unresolved: Withhold a datetime policy because its treatment of zone changes and ambiguous drafts is not internally clear.

filters.instructions: Select a closed common filter profile appropriate to the actual collection promises and shared browser/MCP/export checks.

criteria.finite: Specify the listed equality, comparisons and null tests together with inclusive endpoints and explicit money currencies. This retains promised date/money functionality and entails typed envelope validation.
criteria.equality_only: Offer only equality and null tests for the supported types. Fewer operations simplify validation, but stated date-range filtering must wait.
criteria.broader: Include typed membership and text-match operations as well. More exploratory queries become possible, at the cost of defining further type/null/grant/index boundaries.
criteria.unresolved: Decline to choose until the type exclusions and per-field access handling are sufficiently bounded.

labels.instructions: Recommend shared record-instance wording that obeys visible-field grants and does not confuse declaration captions with identities.

criteria.exact_defaults: Choose permitted nonblank title, then name, and otherwise the full-ID/type caption fallback, retaining secondary IDs. This is implicit and compact but does not express every domain-specific identifier.
criteria.id_only: Use complete opaque identities with type captions everywhere. Field selection is unnecessary and reads are minimal, though human identification is cumbersome.
criteria.authored: Permit a typed checked instance-label declaration plus the identity fallback. Business-specific naming is precise, but a new notation and per-model decisions are required.
criteria.unresolved: Defer the label rule if distinct choices or unreadable destinations cannot be handled without disclosure.

coherent.instructions: Does this limited proposal form a consistent draft contract when server authorization stays authoritative, source-refresh delegation is not invented, query/control types are finite, datetime ambiguity is explicit, labels use current grants and runtime implementation remains absent?
